title: Annotatio III §.II: From the Lutheran side — Luther himself urges Bucer toward Concord (1535); then presses Strasbourg and Swiss approvals (1536–1538)
pass_a_gloss: There is added to the Perfection of the Wittenberg Concord from the LUTHERAN side, that Bucer was spurred by Luther himself toward seeking this Concord, by Letters given to the Strasburgers, in the Year 1535, in Buddeus Epistle 120, p. 248; After the Formula of Concord was established, Luther pressed the approval of the Strasburgers in the Year 1536, Epistle 223, p. 257, and also of the Helvetians in the Year 1537, December 1, Epistle 231, and in the Year 1538, Epistle 232.
pass_b_english: From the Lutheran side, another mark of the Wittenberg Concord’s completeness is this: Luther himself spurred Bucer to seek it — letters to the Strasburgers, 1535 (Buddeus, Epistle 120, p. 248).
After the Formula was set, Luther pressed Strasbourg’s approval in 1536 (Epistle 223, p. 257), and the Swiss as well — 1 December 1537 (Epistle 231) and 1538 (Epistle 232).
source_text: Accedit ad Perfectionem Concordiae Wittenbergensis à parte LUTHERANORUM, Bucerum ad hanc Concordiam quaerendam, à Luthero ipso incitatum fuisse, Literis ad Argentinenses datis, Anno 1535. apud Buddeum Epist. 120. pag. 248.; Post Formulam Concordiae constitutam, approbationem Argentinensium Anno 1536. Lutherum ursisse, Epistola 223. pag. 257. etiam Helvetiorum Anno 1537. 1. Decembr. Epist. 231 & Anno 1538. Epist. 232.
notes: Hexades Annotatio III §.II densify §205; Lutheran-side letter trail 1535–1538.
